observation.visible_scene: A bright dance studio with white walls, a light wood floor, a dark ceiling with track lights and a wall air-conditioner unit, and a large floor-to-ceiling mirror on the right. A woman in a teal traditional-style tunic with a green sash and white trousers stands with her back to the camera, facing the mirror, so her front view appears as a reflection. She holds a red folding fan. The camera and background stay fixed; the only moving entity is the dancer and her reflection.
visible_changes: At the start the red fan is held low, near the waist/hip, oriented roughly edge-on (a thin horizontal red line in the reflection), with the dancer's right arm bent at her side.

Within the first ~0.1–0.2 s the fan in the reflection changes from that thin horizontal line into a wider curved red arc with a dark inner edge, i.e. the fan opens / reorients from closed to open while still held at waist level.
From about t=0.48 s onward the dancer's arms begin to lift, drawing the open red fan upward along her torso toward the shoulders; the right hand rises from the hip to mid-back.

By about t=0.80–0.92 s both hands are raised above the head, holding the fan horizontally behind the neck/head with elbows flared outward, and this raised pose is sustained through the last frame (t=1.6 s).
The mirror reflection reproduces every stage of this motion (front view of the same person), not a separate figure.
Near the end (t≈1.5–1.6 s) the reflection shows a slight shift/flare of the white trousers, suggesting a small weight shift or body sway, while the raised-arm pose is maintained.
No camera movement is evident; the lighting fixtures, AC unit and mirror seams remain in identical positions across all frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the fan-raising is part of a larger choreographic sequence and what precedes or follows this excerpt.
The exact hand manipulation that opens the fan (the transition is brief and partly obscured).
The position of the dancer's left arm from the rear view, since it is largely hidden by her torso.
uncertain_details: Whether the early change in the red shape is a true fan opening or merely a change in viewing orientation of a partly open fan.
Whether the small end-of-clip trouser movement is a turn, a step, or just fabric settling.
The precise moment the arms reach the final overhead position (the change is gradual between ~0.8 and ~1.0 s).
